summary: Brick light on Pumpkin Island at the western end of Eggemoggin Reach, Maine: built 1854 (first exhibited 1855 per LighthouseFriends), discontinued 1933, sold 1934, private and closed to visitors.

notes_for_editor: Revision pass on the earlier draft. LighthouseFriends quotations cut to short phrases (copyrighted-source limit). The 1852 Coast Survey recommendation and the 1923 Judge Peters letter are cited as quoted by LighthouseFriends; neither original was read. The Whitehead fog-signal note is in the 1893-94 bound volume at scan 754 (corpus label 1894); the story gives no year for it. The February 1899 discontinuance is at scan 34 (confirmed by corpus page search). The 1916 list (scan 165) is cited for the name only; its table layout is jumbled. Bulletin 1921 p. 32 (July 1921 rescue of two women and children) is column-jumbled OCR; positions matched by reading the column text; the checker reads the page image for it. Conflicts left open: first year (NRHP 1854 established; LighthouseFriends first exhibited 1 Jan 1855); tower height (NRHP 22 ft to lantern middle; LighthouseFriends 17 ft to lantern deck); focal plane (LighthouseFriends 27 ft; the station record's 13.1 m is unverified); end of service (LighthouseFriends January 1933; NRHP dry-ledge beacon replaced the station in 1934). Name variants: roster John C. Tibbets vs LighthouseFriends John Chester Tibbetts; roster J. G. Walker (1861-1864) is included. Charles S. Holt (1902-1911) is attested only by the roster and LighthouseFriends; the Allen C. Holt in the Bulletins is a keeper at Deer Island Thorofare and is not the same person. Pumpkin Island Reef (flashing acetylene light, 1916) is a different aid and is not used. The 1934 sale price and buyer are from LighthouseFriends only. Babson's war wound and the 1923 telephone letter are LighthouseFriends only. No Pumpkin Island newspaper search was done (the Chronicling America search timed out on the Sharps Island run). Board labels: the list of changes at scan 27 is the January 1893 entry; the February 1894 entry at scan 318 is in the 1894 part of the same bound volume. Fact-check 2026-10-22 (second pass): the 1921 Bulletin pages were read as page images (rendered from the cached 1921 PDF). Page 16 (printed p. 176) confirms the 17 March 1921 entry: Newman 'rendered assistance to a disabled power boat, with one man aboard, which had gone ashore in the vicinity of the light station.' Page 32 (printed p. 192) confirms the commendation 'for the rescue on July 1 of two women and children adrift in a rowboat.' The Commissioner FY1921 entry (scan 663) describes a disabled power boat with one occupant offshore; the story says the two entries may describe the same boat. The NRHP spells the island 'Little Dear Isle' (a typo; the story uses Little Deer Isle, as LighthouseFriends and the USLHS place record do). The USLHS place record gives the light 43 ft above mean high water; LighthouseFriends gives a 27 ft focal plane (about 8.2 m), so the existing focal-height correction (13.1 m) remains unverified and is not applied. The Board fog-signal note (scan 754), the 1893 and 1894 ice closures (scan 27, 318) and the 1899 closure (scan 34) are confirmed. The 1854 and 1855 first-year conflict is kept open. The footnoted accessed dates (2026-10-23) post-date the 2026-10-22 check date and should be reconciled.
